core_obligations: Reduce the question to an affine chart X = Spec(A) with A a finite type k-algebra and x corresponding to a prime ideal (proof lines 2553-2556).
Prove the forward direction: localize so that A is smooth over k, then k' tensor A is smooth over k' for every extension and each of these Noetherian rings is regular (proof lines 2559-2563).

Prove the converse: choose a finite purely inseparable extension k' making the compositum of k' with the residue field at x separable over k', use uniqueness of the prime above to identify the residue field at the lifted prime, conclude smoothness over k' from regularity plus separability, and descend smoothness to k (proof lines 2565-2582).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an affine chart (proof lines 2553-2556).
Forward direction by field extension (proof lines 2559-2563).
Converse by a purely inseparable base change that separates the residue field (proof lines 2565-2582).
difficulty_reason: For a scheme X locally of finite type over a field k and a point x, the lemma proves that geometric regularity at x is equivalent to smoothness of X over k at x (statement lines 2543-2550). One direction is immediate: localizing to an affine chart, smoothness over k survives arbitrary field extensions and makes each of the Noetherian rings involved regular (proof lines 2559-2563). The converse is the substantive direction and is a purely inseparable trick: taking the residue field K at x, which is finitely generated over k, one finds a finite purely inseparable extension k' such that the compositum k'K is separable over k'; because the prime lifted to k' tensor A is the unique prime over the original one, its residue field is exactly that compositum, so regularity of the base changed local ring plus separability makes k' to A' smooth at the lifted prime, and smoothness descends back along the purely inseparable field extension (proof lines 2565-2582). The claim is H2: three cited algebra inputs, but the choice of the purely inseparable extension and the uniqueness of the prime above are what make the argument work.
